story.title: The “Nobody Else Knows” Moment
paragraphs: You’re doing something completely ordinary. Paying the mortgage. Looking for an insurance document.
Then the thought hits you:
“If something happened to me, nobody would even know this needed doing.”
And the realization follows: I’m the one who knows.
My spouse doesn’t know my phone passcode. He doesn’t know where the life insurance policy is filed. He wouldn’t know which account pays the mortgage, or how to access the utility bills.
“If something happened to me tonight, my husband would have to start sorting all of this, and he doesn’t even know which bank I use.”
It’s a heavy, invisible load. The responsibility you never meant to carry alone could leave absolute chaos behind when the people you love need it least.
You’ve been meaning to sort it out for years, but life simply gets in the way.

alternatives.title: The uncomfortable truth we secretly know

items.title: “I’ll do it later”
paragraphs: But later never comes. Meanwhile, there are more accounts, more policies, more documents — and that background anxiety grows louder.

items.title: Scattered Notes
paragraphs: Passwords in your phone notes. Documents in “that drawer.”
This isn’t a system. It’s a scavenger hunt for your family.

items.title: Notes Apps
paragraphs: Disorganised, and usually just turns into the Netflix password and a grocery list.
Not secure. Not structured. Not enough.

items.title: The Expensive Lawyer
paragraphs: $2,000+ and it covers the legal side.
But it doesn’t tell your husband how to pay the water bill or what the Wi-Fi password is.

solution.title: What If Your Family Had One Place To Look?
paragraphs: One organised binder.
Clear sections.
Simple prompts.
The important information together instead of spread across your phone, laptop, drawers and memory.
So if somebody ever needs it, they’re not trying to piece everything together themselves.
They know where to start.

product.subtitle: The “If I’m Not Here” Binder

items.title: Master Account Index
paragraphs: Bank accounts, savings, credit cards and investments.
What exists and where to find it.

items.title: Insurance Control Hub

Policies, providers and contact details together.

items.title: Digital Access Guide
paragraphs: Phone access, email, important logins and online accounts.
The things that become surprisingly difficult when the person who set them up isn’t there.

Which account it comes from.
When it goes out.
So nobody is finding out about an important payment because it suddenly stopped.

Medical information.
Important possessions.
Digital assets.
And the practical details that are obvious to you because you deal with them every day.

items.title: “We have loads of accounts”
paragraphs: Then there’s more for somebody else to figure out.
The sections can grow with you.

items.title: “Our finances are complicated”
paragraphs: They don’t need to be simple.
They need to be understandable to someone other than you.

items.title: “What about security?”
paragraphs: You decide where the finished copy lives.
Keep one somewhere safe at home, keep a protected digital copy, or share it only with the person you trust.
Your information stays under your control.

items.title: “My husband knows most of this”
paragraphs: Maybe he does.
But if you weren’t there to answer questions, would he know where to find it?
That’s the difference.

mechanism.title: Why this works better than starting with a blank notebook

items.title: It Prompts You

The questions are already there.

items.title: It Organises It

They don’t need to understand your filing system first.

items.title: It Covers The Awkward Bits
paragraphs: The things you normally only discover matter when there’s a problem.

“I didn’t know that.”
Then put the finished copy somewhere safe.
If, within 60 days, you don’t feel it was worth the money to finally have this sorted, send us an email and we’ll refund you.
Simple.
We think the bigger surprise will be how long you left it.

bump.title: YES — ADD THE “FIRST 48 HOURS” CRISIS CHECKLIST
paragraphs: Having the information is one thing.
Knowing what to do first is another.
When something serious happens, nobody wants to be Googling:
“What do I do now?”
The First 48 Hours Crisis Checklist gives your family a simple order to follow.
Who needs to be contacted first.
What can wait.
Which financial accounts you don’t want to rush into closing.
What needs attention during the first couple of days.
Something practical to follow when nobody feels particularly capable of thinking.

items.title: Is it digital?
paragraphs: Yes.
You get a digital version you can complete on screen and a version you can print.
A lot of people will want both: one they can update and one kept somewhere safe.

items.title: Does this replace a will?
paragraphs: No.
A will deals with legal decisions.
This deals with the practical information somebody would need to find and understand your everyday life.
You may need both.

items.title: How long will it take?
paragraphs: You can get most of the important sections done in an evening.
Some things may take longer simply because you need to look them up.
You don’t have to finish every field before it becomes useful.

final.title: Stop Keeping All Of This In Your Head
paragraphs: You’ve probably been meaning to sort it out.
You already know why it matters.
This just gives you a simple way to finally do it.
For them.
And, actually, for you too.
